title: Reversal of Redemptions on Voided Tickets — Crestline Flight Credits and Travel Vouchers
content:
**Accounting rule.** When a ticket paid with value from Crestline Flight Credits and Travel Vouchers is voided inside the ticket's risk-free window, the value of each redemption on that ticket returns to the credit it came from. It returns in one reversal entry per redemption and keeps that credit's expiry date.

**Conditions of a reversal.**
- A redemption is reversed only when the ticket it paid for has status voided. The ticket's status in the system record, matched by the ticket number the redemption paid for, is the evidence.
- Each redemption can be reversed at most once. The evidence is whether a reversal entry already stands against that redemption entry.

**Effects of a reversal.**
- A reversal that gives a depleted credit value again makes it active.
- A remainder that was forfeited under the single-use rule is not restored by the reversal.

**What is not a reversal.** A ticket paid with credit that is refunded or cancelled for credit after the risk-free window does not reverse the redemption. Its value comes back as a new credit under the credit redeposit rule instead.

## Ledger view (hypothetical)

| Situation on the ticket paid with credit | Ledger effect on the credit that paid |
|---|---|
| Ticket voided inside the risk-free window; two redemptions from two credits | One reversal entry on each credit, for the value that credit paid; each keeps its expiry date |
| Ticket voided; the redemption already has a reversal entry | No second reversal |
| Ticket voided; the paying credit had a 40.00 remainder forfeited after the redemption | The redemption value returns; the 40.00 forfeited remainder does not |
| Ticket refunded after the risk-free window | No reversal; value returns as a new credit by redeposit |

A depleted credit that receives a reversal of 150.00 US dollars becomes active with 150.00 of value. The figure is hypothetical.
